items.stem: Why is the checks-effects-interactions pattern important when sending Ether out of a contract?

options.text: Updating state before the external call prevents a reentrant call from draining funds
options.rationale: Correct: state is settled before control leaves the contract.

options.text: It makes the contract compile faster
options.rationale: It is a security pattern, not a compile optimisation.

options.text: It reduces the deployment bytecode size
options.rationale: Its purpose is reentrancy safety, not size.

options.text: It lets the contract skip gas payment

items.explanation: Correct: state is settled before control leaves the contract.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid reasons to prefer custom errors over long require strings in Solidity? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Custom errors typically cost less gas than storing revert strings
options.rationale: Correct: custom errors are more gas-efficient.

options.text: Custom errors can carry structured parameters for off-chain decoding
options.rationale: Correct: they can include typed arguments.
They are a way to revert, not to disable reverting.

options.text: Custom errors remove the need for access control
options.rationale: They are unrelated to access control.

items.explanation: Correct: custom errors are more gas-efficient.

items.stem: A function marked `public` that only internal code should call is a problem because:

options.text: External accounts can call it directly, bypassing intended control flow
options.rationale: Correct: public visibility exposes it to external callers.

options.text: Public functions always run out of gas

items.explanation: Correct: public visibility exposes it to external callers.
